alternatives.root_cause: A feature flag was flipped enabling a deliberately slow cart-store code path.
alternatives.why_not: Plausible as the trigger - flagd has an empty change log and cart evaluates a boolean flag on every request - but flagd returned no logs at all in the window, so the flip itself is unconfirmed; and the observed failing mechanism is waiting on a slow store call, which is dependency_latency regardless of what toggled it.

alternatives.root_cause: Cart's Valkey backend is resource-starved (connections or threads) causing serialised 300ms waits.
alternatives.why_not: Exhaustion produces variable, queue-shaped latency and usually errors or refusals; here every operation lands on an identical ~300ms floor with zero errors, which looks injected rather than contended.

alternatives.root_cause: A bad cart image reintroduced the slow store path.
alternatives.why_not: tr_946e36fd442f shows cart's only image changes were about 24h before onset and both were reverted, leaving no artifact change near the incident window.

verdict.summary: Cart's Valkey cart-store operations each stall at a uniform ~300ms floor, adding ~600ms to every checkout and pushing latency up through checkout, frontend, frontend-proxy and the load generator.
verdict.reasoning: In tr_87fabe12aa66 every trace shows the same signature: cart/HGET, cart/HMSET and cart/EXPIRE each consume almost exactly 300ms of self-time, while every other dependency (currency, product-catalog, shipping, quote, payment, email, flagd) returns in under a few milliseconds. The quantised, identical 300ms per store operation indicates injected delay in cart's store call path, not organic load. Cart is alive and serving (tr_3497bfcf84bf shows continuous, normal, error-free log activity across the window), which rules out freeze, partition and disk fill, and nothing in its logs indicates decode failures or resource exhaustion. The incident is latency, not errors: checkout's error ratio is flat at zero in the window (tr_c610bae4d1ac) and cart emitted no error-ratio samples at all (tr_189d126c8053), so callers are alerting on slow responses propagating upward from cart. Cart's only recorded changes are ~24 hours before onset and were reverted (tr_946e36fd442f), and flagd has no change records and no logs in the window (tr_02ab6796162f, tr_69e7cb62f4d9), consistent with a runtime-toggled slow path rather than a new artifact.
open_questions: Whether the 300ms per-operation delay originates in cart's own code path (e.g. a toggled slow-path) or in the Valkey/cart-store backend itself, since the store was not inspected directly.
The exact onset timestamp for the cart latency, as cart produced no error-ratio samples and no latency metric was pulled.
Whether any flag store state changed at onset - flagd produced neither change records nor logs, so a flip could not be confirmed or excluded.
